title: 3534. Path Existence Queries in a Graph II

examples.explanation: The resulting graph is: Query Shortest Path Minimum Distance [0, 3] 0 → 3 1 [2, 4] 2 → 4 1 Thus, the output is [1, 1].
The resulting graph is: Query Shortest Path Minimum Distance [0, 1] 0 → 1 1 [0, 2] 0 → 1 → 2 2 [2, 3] None -1 [4, 3] 3 → 4 1 Thus, the output is [1, 2, -1, 1].

There are no edges between any two nodes because: Nodes 0 and 1: |nums[0] - nums[1]| = |3 - 6| = 3 > 1 Nodes 0 and 2: |nums[0] - nums[2]| = |3 - 1| = 2 > 1 Nodes 1 and 2: |nums[1] - nums[2]| = |6 - 1| = 5 > 1 Thus, no node can reach any other node, and the output is [0, -1, -1].
